content.title: A tested migration path to post-quantum KL-HSM signing

facts.text: Kriptolog reports limited microcontroller flash and RAM, ARM Cortex-M firmware in C, and firmware architecture not yet adapted for larger keys or different signature flows. Its listed technologies include PKCS#11.

sources.quote: Our HSM firmware runs on a constrained microcontroller with limited flash and RAM, so a straight drop-in is not possible.
Custom ARM Cortex-M firmware in C for HSM cryptographic operations
we have not touched the firmware architecture to accommodate larger key material or different signature flows.

facts.text: The company's migration enquiry concerns firmware versions, performance trade-offs and hybrid transition operation, with a twelve-month planning horizon for a roadmap and integration proof of concept.

sources.quote: which firmware version will support post-quantum algorithms, what the performance trade-offs are
how hybrid classical/post-quantum operation will work during transition.
A good outcome is a documented roadmap and at least one working proof-of-concept integration inside twelve months.

facts.text: Kriptolog's plans state an end-2025 Common Criteria EAL4+ objective for the KL-500; that statement does not establish current certification status.

sources.quote: Kriptolog intends to achieve Common Criteria EAL4+ certification for the KL-500 HSM by the end of 2025

facts.text: Kriptolog reports a twelve-engineer core R&D group and modest capacity for collaboration.

sources.quote: We have a core R&D group of twelve engineers
with modest capacity to take on collaborative projects if the scope is well-defined and the output is practically applicable.

facts.text: Nikolić's work implements Dilithium and Falcon signatures on an STM32F407 Cortex-M4. Separate Dilithium research reports compiler-dependent leakage. Her hybrid HSM prototype concerns ECDH plus Kyber key exchange, rather than hybrid signing.

sources.quote: We implement the NIST post-quantum signature finalists CRYSTALS-Dilithium (security levels 2 and 3) and Falcon-512 in C
on an STM32F407 board running at 168 MHz.
Leakage detection using Welch's t-test and TVLA methodology crosses the threshold of |t| = 4.5 in three of eight compiler/architecture combinations.
Full key exchange (hybrid ECDH + Kyber-768) completes in 38 ms end-to-end.

facts.text: The researcher's notes describe a preference for real hardware and measurable deliverables. Her laboratory has two SLE97 evaluation kits, with limited availability.

sources.quote: Prefers collaborative arrangements that involve real hardware and measurable deliverables rather than purely theoretical work.
The lab has limited availability of the Infineon SLE97 evaluation kits (two units); industrial partners providing additional hardware would accelerate shared projects.

facts.text: Nikolić's stated participation interests include joint projects with companies developing HSMs.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies developing HSMs, IoT security firmware, or industrial control system security

inferences: Her signature benchmarking experience suggests a strong methodological fit, but earlier Dilithium results cannot establish final ML-DSA correctness, memory fit or security on KL-HSM hardware.

Hybrid key-exchange experience likely helps architecture discussions, but signing policy, PKCS#11 integration and client verifier compatibility need separate validation. Compiler-dependent leakage is a material implementation risk.

This joint-project proposal is conditional because Nikolić's current availability is unknown. A narrowly bounded hardware pilot likely fits the company's collaborative capacity better than an immediate product-wide migration.
proposedActions: Propose an initial eight-week experiment on one agreed KL-HSM variant using its production toolchain. Kriptolog would supply development hardware, builds, its prototype and non-production keys; Nikolić would lead porting and measurement. Compare current RSA/ECDSA operation with standards-conformant ML-DSA and a defined hybrid flow using known-answer vectors and representative signing workloads. Separate tuning and held-out evaluation workloads and verify independence before selecting the best configuration. Measure correctness, peak RAM, flash, p99 latency, throughput, PKCS#11/verifier interoperability and preliminary timing leakage. Proposed go/no-go requires all correctness and interoperability tests passing, measured resource use and performance within pre-agreed numerical limits, and no detected leakage under an agreed adequately powered screen. Insufficient evidence means unresolved, not pass. Assess the best configuration against these criteria, not against a preferred algorithm. Include a feasibility review of delivery within twelve months; functional success would not establish production security or certification.

Propose months three through twelve for a bounded integration proof of concept and versioned roadmap covering key storage, signature flows, hybrid policy, client compatibility and measured trade-offs. Review deliverables against the company's twelve-month outcome, firmware-version information and performance-reporting needs. Include certification change-impact review and agreed side-channel/fault testing; unresolved security or evaluator requirements would block production-readiness claims.

Agree a small, practically applicable work package with named company and researcher effort, budget, hardware access and confidentiality/licensing terms. Prioritise representative KL-HSM hardware; schedule within the two-kit availability limit if SLE97 comparisons are justified, or negotiate partner-supplied units. Reconfirm scope and schedule after the initial experiment.

What initial KL-HSM variant, hardware/build access, company engineering allocation and budget can support the pilot?
What agreed acceptance specification defines signing scope, ML-DSA parameters, resource and performance ceilings, hybrid policy, PKCS#11 consumers and client verifiers?
What is the KL-500's current certification status and the applicable evaluator-approved change-control, side-channel and fault-testing scope?

content.markdown:
# A tested migration path to post-quantum KL-HSM signing

## Verified facts
- Kriptolog reports limited microcontroller flash and RAM, ARM Cortex-M firmware in C, and firmware architecture not yet adapted for larger keys or different signature flows. Its listed technologies include PKCS#11. [F1]
- The company's migration enquiry concerns firmware versions, performance trade-offs and hybrid transition operation, with a twelve-month planning horizon for a roadmap and integration proof of concept. [F2]
- Kriptolog's plans state an end-2025 Common Criteria EAL4+ objective for the KL-500; that statement does not establish current certification status. [F3]
- Kriptolog reports a twelve-engineer core R&D group and modest capacity for collaboration. [F4]
- Nikolić's work implements Dilithium and Falcon signatures on an STM32F407 Cortex-M4. Separate Dilithium research reports compiler-dependent leakage. Her hybrid HSM prototype concerns ECDH plus Kyber key exchange, rather than hybrid signing. [F5]
- The researcher's notes describe a preference for real hardware and measurable deliverables. Her laboratory has two SLE97 evaluation kits, with limited availability. [F6]
- Nikolić's stated participation interests include joint projects with companies developing HSMs. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The first experiment could distinguish a feasible firmware migration from changes requiring architectural redesign, giving clients a more defensible account of resource costs, compatibility and release dependencies.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and access, Nikolić could test how earlier signature implementation methods transfer to production HSM firmware, using target-hardware measurements to study resource, toolchain and security trade-offs.

## Our inference
- Her signature benchmarking experience suggests a strong methodological fit, but earlier Dilithium results cannot establish final ML-DSA correctness, memory fit or security on KL-HSM hardware.
- Hybrid key-exchange experience likely helps architecture discussions, but signing policy, PKCS#11 integration and client verifier compatibility need separate validation. Compiler-dependent leakage is a material implementation risk.
- This joint-project proposal is conditional because Nikolić's current availability is unknown. A narrowly bounded hardware pilot likely fits the company's collaborative capacity better than an immediate product-wide migration.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose an initial eight-week experiment on one agreed KL-HSM variant using its production toolchain. Kriptolog would supply development hardware, builds, its prototype and non-production keys; Nikolić would lead porting and measurement. Compare current RSA/ECDSA operation with standards-conformant ML-DSA and a defined hybrid flow using known-answer vectors and representative signing workloads. Separate tuning and held-out evaluation workloads and verify independence before selecting the best configuration. Measure correctness, peak RAM, flash, p99 latency, throughput, PKCS#11/verifier interoperability and preliminary timing leakage. Proposed go/no-go requires all correctness and interoperability tests passing, measured resource use and performance within pre-agreed numerical limits, and no detected leakage under an agreed adequately powered screen. Insufficient evidence means unresolved, not pass. Assess the best configuration against these criteria, not against a preferred algorithm. Include a feasibility review of delivery within twelve months; functional success would not establish production security or certification.
- Propose months three through twelve for a bounded integration proof of concept and versioned roadmap covering key storage, signature flows, hybrid policy, client compatibility and measured trade-offs. Review deliverables against the company's twelve-month outcome, firmware-version information and performance-reporting needs. Include certification change-impact review and agreed side-channel/fault testing; unresolved security or evaluator requirements would block production-readiness claims.
- Agree a small, practically applicable work package with named company and researcher effort, budget, hardware access and confidentiality/licensing terms. Prioritise representative KL-HSM hardware; schedule within the two-kit availability limit if SLE97 comparisons are justified, or negotiate partner-supplied units. Reconfirm scope and schedule after the initial experiment.

## Open questions
- Can Nikolić confirm availability and researcher/laboratory effort for this proposed twelve-month joint project?
- What initial KL-HSM variant, hardware/build access, company engineering allocation and budget can support the pilot?
- What agreed acceptance specification defines signing scope, ML-DSA parameters, resource and performance ceilings, hybrid policy, PKCS#11 consumers and client verifiers?
- What is the KL-500's current certification status and the applicable evaluator-approved change-control, side-channel and fault-testing scope?
